from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Vectors are arrows from origin to points.",
            "Combine vectors by scaling and adding.",
            "This creates new vectors in space.",
            "The robot arm shows reachability.",
            "Linear combinations define movement space."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites & Linear Combinations", lecture_lines)
        
        # Load assets
        robot_svg = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg")
        
        # Create vectors
        v1 = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT + UP, color=BLUE)
        v2 = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 0.5 + DOWN * 1.5, color=GREEN)
        vector_group = VGroup(v1, v2)
        
        # Positioning
        self.place_at_grid(v1, 'B2', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(v2, 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_in_area(vector_group, 'C4', 'F6', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(v1), FadeIn(v2), FadeIn(robot_svg))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Scalar multiplication
        v1_scaled = Arrow(ORIGIN, (RIGHT + UP) * 1.5, color=BLUE)
        self.play(Transform(v1, v1_scaled))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        v_sum = Vector(v1.get_end() + v2.get_end(), color=YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(v_sum))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Visualizing robot arm movement
        self.place_at_grid(robot_svg, 'D4', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Indicate(robot_svg))
        self.lecture[3].set_color(RED)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(FadeOut(robot_svg), FadeOut(v1), FadeOut(v2), FadeOut(v_sum))
        self.lecture[4].set_color(ORANGE)
        self.wait(1)

    def construct(self):

            "Independent vectors add new dimensions.",

        ])

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Span defines total reachable space.",
            "Dependence measures system efficiency.",
            "Basis provides minimal coordinates."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Application", lecture_lines)
        
        # Load assets
        grid_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg")
        protractor_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/protractor.svg")

        # Define visual elements
        span_box = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        span_text = Text("Reach", font_size=24)
        span_group = VGroup(span_box, span_text)

        dep_box = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=YELLOW).set_fill(YELLOW, opacity=0.3)
        dep_text = Text("Efficiency", font_size=24)
        dep_group = VGroup(dep_box, dep_text)

        basis_box = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=GREEN).set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.3)
        basis_text = Text("Coordinates", font_size=24)
        basis_group = VGroup(basis_box, basis_text)

        # Coordinate system example
        axes = ThreeDAxes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], z_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        axes_label = Text("Basis vectors define space", font_size=20, color="#AAAAAA")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(span_group, 'C2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(grid_icon, 'B1', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(span_group), FadeIn(grid_icon))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(dep_group, 'C5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(dep_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(basis_group, 'D3', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Create(basis_group))
        
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'E1', 'F4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(axes_label, 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(protractor_icon, 'E6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(axes_label), FadeIn(protractor_icon))

outline.topic: Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Spans to Bases

sections.title: Prerequisites & Linear Combinations
sections.content: Define vectors as arrows in space (origin to point). Explain Linear Combination as 'scaling and adding' vectors: c1v1 + c2v2. Visualization: Use a coordinate grid to show how vectors reach different points.
sections.example: A robot arm has two joints. Joint 1 moves vector A, Joint 2 moves vector B. The robot's hand reaches any point that is a combination of these movements.

sections.title: The Concept of Span
sections.content: Define Span as the set of all possible points reachable via linear combinations. Visualize this as the 'footprint' of vectors: a line (1 vector), a plane (2 non-collinear vectors), or 3D space (3 non-coplanar vectors).
sections.example: If two vectors point in the same direction, they only span a line. If they point in different directions, they 'sweep out' a flat 2D carpet (plane).

sections.title: Linear Dependence vs. Independence
sections.content: Explain Linear Dependence as 'redundancy.' If one vector can be formed by others, it is redundant. If no vector can be formed by the others, they are independent. Visual cue: 'Collapsing' dimensions when vectors are redundant.
sections.example: Three hikers walking in a line: If Hiker C follows Hiker B, Hiker C is redundant (linearly dependent). If Hiker C moves in a new direction, they add a new dimension of freedom.

sections.title: Bases: The Minimum Building Blocks
sections.content: Define a Basis as the minimal set of vectors that span the entire space. It must be linearly independent and span the space. This is the 'DNA' of the vector space.
sections.example: Using standard basis vectors i=(1,0) and j=(0,1) as the 'grid' map that allows you to define any coordinate in a city grid.

sections.title: Summary & Application
sections.content: Synthesize: Span is the 'reach,' Dependence is the 'efficiency,' and Basis is the 'minimal coordinate system.' Connect this to data science where bases represent dimensions of features.
sections.example: In 3D video games, the basis vectors define the world's axis; without them, the game engine wouldn't know how to place objects in space.
